about.title: Rialto Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A faulty product does not care where you live, but the aftermath plays out close to home. In Rialto, that might mean an emergency visit after a space heater catches fire, a child seat that failed during a collision on Baseline Road, or a power tool that came apart in a garage off Riverside Avenue. California product liability claims often rest on strict liability: you generally need to show the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury. Proving the company was careless is usually not required. The list of who may answer for the harm is also wider than the name on the box. Manufacturers, distributors, and the retailer that sold the item in San Bernardino County can each carry responsibility. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Rialto residents, free of charge, with an independent attorney who takes these claims on contingency. Keep the product, keep the packaging, and reach out when you are ready.

whyChoose.title: Why Rialto Residents Use LawProactive for Product Claims

items.title: Strict Liability Changes the Question
items.desc: In California, a defective product case usually turns on whether the item was flawed and caused your injury, not on whether the maker meant to cut corners. The attorneys in our network build cases around that standard.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving the Product
items.desc: The item that hurt you is often the single most important piece of evidence. From your first call, you will hear how to keep it, its packaging, and any receipts intact rather than tossing them out.

items.title: More Than One Responsible Party
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the store that sold the product may all share liability under California law. An independent attorney can identify each of them so no responsible party is overlooked.

items.question: My airbag did not deploy in a crash on SR-210 near Rialto. Is that a product case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Rialto recorded 432 injury collisions in 2025, and some of those involve a vehicle part that did not perform the way it was supposed to. If an airbag, seatbelt, or tire failed, the vehicle or component manufacturer may be liable under strict liability in addition to any driver who caused the crash. Ask the repair shop not to discard the parts until an attorney has reviewed the situation.

items.question: Do I have to show the company knew the product was defective?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability often runs on strict liability, meaning you typically need to establish that the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury. The company's state of mind is usually not the issue. An attorney can explain how that standard applies to the specific item that hurt you.

items.question: I bought the product at a store in Rialto, not directly from the manufacturer. Who is responsible?
items.answer: Under California law, retailers and distributors can be held liable alongside the manufacturer, even if they never touched the design. That matters when a maker is overseas or hard to locate. Save your receipt or bank record showing where in San Bernardino County you bought the item, since it helps establish the chain of sale.
